subject.title: fix(gateway): require shared secret for tailscale serve auth

question: Should core permanently support an opt-in mode that requires both OpenClaw-verified Tailscale identity and a Gateway token/password, rather than directing hardened deployments to `allowTailscale: false` with shared-secret auth?
rationale: Both approaches require a shared secret, but the PR adds config and session semantics to preserve app-layer Tailscale identity and attribution; repository policy cannot determine whether that additional security contract is worth the permanent surface.

options.title: Use Existing Hardening Path
options.body: Decline the new config surface and strengthen documentation for `allowTailscale: false` with token/password unless app-layer identity retention is an explicit requirement.

options.title: Approve Layered Authentication
options.body: Accept the new opt-in contract after current-head real Gateway proof and explicit approval of session invalidation and upgrade semantics.

recommendation.title: Use Existing Hardening Path
recommendation.body: Decline the new config surface and strengthen documentation for `allowTailscale: false` with token/password unless app-layer identity retention is an explicit requirement.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history ties steipete to the existing Tailscale Gateway-auth behavior and its documented security boundary.
